label: SITL 17 INT carrier goto
info:
First live COMMAND_INT flight: Arm → Takeoff (LONG, PX4 default altitude) → DO_REPOSITION on the INT carrier against PX4 SITL sysid 11.

The proof: the goto node is configured in decimal degrees (47.3991, 8.5456 — about 150 m north of the PX4 SITL default home). On the wire those must become degE7 int32s (x=473991000, y=85456000) with an explicit frame. If the scaling were wrong the vehicle would reject the frame or aim at null island; repositioning to the correct nearby point is the proof.

Flight-validated (2026-07): three ACCEPTED acks, arrival at 47.399100 / 8.545603 — within ~0.2 m of the configured target — with altitude held (~491 m AMSL) throughout the transit. Note the target is an absolute coordinate, not a home-relative offset: a rig whose home spawns off the classic Zurich default flies a correspondingly shorter or longer leg (~135 m on the validation flight).

Prerequisites: the Docker lab's PX4 stack (bind 14560 → remote 14561, sysid 11), vehicle disarmed on the ground.

Altitude is NaN — deliberately. PX4's DO_REPOSITION reads param7/z as metres AMSL no matter what MAV_FRAME the COMMAND_INT carries: mavlink_receiver drops the frame when it builds the internal vehicle_command (that uORB message has no frame field), and the navigator copies z straight into an AMSL setpoint. A "relative" 20 therefore means 20 m AMSL — about 468 m underground at the 488 m Zurich home — and PX4 still acks ACCEPTED, then descends into the ground a few metres into the transit (observed on this flow's first live flight: accepted, ~16 m of northward travel, early land + disarm). Non-finite z is PX4's own escape hatch: the navigator holds current altitude. The node config carries it as the JSON string "NaN", which the param merger coerces to a real NaN sentinel (the takeoff node shows the other route — injecting NaN via a runtime payload).

Troubleshooting:
- Arm DENIED → the rig's RC-loss config (the Docker entrypoint sets this; for a hand-built PX4, set COM_RCL_EXCEPT to allow offboard/hold without RC).
- Goto accepted but the vehicle descends/lands instead of holding the transit → z is finite and below terrain; PX4 treats it as AMSL (see above). Keep z NaN, or send terrain-clearing AMSL (~508 m at the Zurich home).
- A COMMAND_LONG_ONLY ack would trigger the one-shot carrier swap back to LONG — also a valid observation, but PX4 speaks INT natively so it should not occur.

name: INT carrier goto (PX4 SITL sysid 11)
info:
Arm and Takeoff ride COMMAND_LONG (the migrated example convention; both are non-positional). The goto is the test subject: carrier = COMMAND_INT, frame = Global relative alt, coordinates entered in decimal degrees per the canonical-degrees doctrine.

Takeoff altitude is passed as NaN via a function node — JSON config cannot express NaN, but the runtime payload can, and NaN in param7 on the LONG carrier means "use the firmware default" (PX4 MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT). Takeoff uses the confirm tier, not complete: the completion condition compares altitude against param7, which NaN would break. An 8 s delay stands in for the climb.

The goto's altitude (param7) is the config string "NaN" — hold current altitude. PX4 ignores the COMMAND_INT frame for DO_REPOSITION's z and reads it as AMSL, so a finite "relative" altitude near ground level aims underground (see the tab description). NaN sidesteps the trap and keeps the flow's proof focused on what the INT carrier actually changes: degE7 lat/lon in x/y.

name: takeoff alt = NaN (PX4 default)
